package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and Kubernetes credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py is executed automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credential files are read from the user's system.

attack_chain.action: The contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config are exfiltrated to an external server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to the user's SSH and Kubernetes credentials.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config.
The package initiates outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com during setup.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
setup.py containing hardcoded references to app.threatest.com
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI packages whose setup.py reads sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config and sends their contents to external domains, specifically app.threatest.com. Flag any package that performs outbound network requests to this domain during installation. Use static analysis to detect hardcoded file paths and network destinations in setup.py.
